title: Roy Eldridge
summary: He met Roy in Cincinnati and jammed with a guitar, and they stayed friends in New York.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: You mentioned Roy Eldridge a little earlier. How did you relate to Roy's style?

I liked Roy. I was in school when I first met Roy. I was touring with the school band through Cincinnati, and Roy was playing with one of the bands there in Cincinnati. I'm trying to think of the name. I can't recall it now. The Cotton Pickers? McKinney Cotton Pickers? I'm not sure that's the band. But, I met him in Cincinnati. And then, when he finished his job and I finished ours, we was in a club at a hotel. So, Roy and I met there and started talking. And we, I don't know how we finally knew each other, but we both had trumpets. So, we got a fellow with a guitar. So, we go upstairs to his room and we started jamming right there between them with
this guitar. And, that's how we happened to kind of know each other from then on through the years.
At that time, Roy was in New York before I got there. When I got to New York, we were so glad to see each other. Roy was there with Teddy Hill. Remember the name Teddy Hill?
Teddy Hill had the band, and Roy was there with Chue Berry and all that when I got there. And then, we met each other during that time. We knew each other.
